items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Willie Umphrey... good clarinet player... he done pulled his clarinet loose... So, when he got through playing, I said, well, what's the matter, Willie? I quit.

ctx.x: Were there some barber shops around the Big 25 or Elk Place or something? Yeah, but I didn't know none of them.

The musicians? And they didn't have no musicians. They didn't hang out? They didn't even bum in the barber shop? No. They bum around the 25-hour ballroom like that, you know. Not no barber shop, no. Well, what about Jimmy Palau? Now Jimmy Palau was a violin player. He was a good violin player. He played with me. Oh, yeah? Yeah, they played with me at Harry Park and Charlie Park. He played violin with me over there. They, uh, uh, they fired, uh, one time they, uh, they had gotten a humbug. He'd gotten a humbug…
Did they ever have any solo players then? No. Did they have any solo players? Solo, no. No. Not as I love, no. No. Tom Mitchell used to tell me about them. He said you didn't have a band on them.

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1959-08-11
items.q: He played with us at Harry Parkers before we got George Backhead.

ctx.x: Did they have some of the blowing instruments too or mostly strings?

They had blowing instruments too, yeah. Oh, the dance band? Yeah, they had, I think Bunk Johnson was playing in one of the bands at that time. Remember Bunk Johnson? Bunk Johnson was playing with the Silver Leaf, I think. Well, I played with the Silver Leaf for a good while. There's spot jobs, you know, up on the Pelican. Who was the leader of that? Uh, uh, Poisey Umphrey. Oh, Percy or was it his father? No, Poisey. Poisey, yeah. Poisey Umphrey. Willie Umphrey. Willie Umphrey. Willie Umphrey, yeah. The clarinet…
Was that the place called, um, later the Entertainers or 101 Ranch? Yeah.
